title: Sep 26 Results + Sep 27 Preview: When You've Been Around, 69% Feels Like a Tuesday
summary: 9-4 record on Sep 26 keeps us rolling—now eyeing Mets-Nationals for Saturday's action

content.value:
## Another Solid Friday in the Books

Look, I've been doing this long enough to know that 9-4 isn't going to make headlines, but it's the kind of day that builds a bankroll. 69.2% accuracy on a 13-game slate? I'll take that every single time. The model hummed along nicely yesterday, and if you've been following our picks, you know we're not chasing perfection—we're chasing value.

## The Hits and Misses

The Dodgers-Giants pick at 63% confidence was textbook—you could see that one coming from a mile away. Same with the Rays sneaking past Philly at 61%. Those are the spots where the data and the eye test align perfectly.

The misses? Well, the Nationals getting one over on us stings a bit, especially since we're going right back to that well tomorrow. The Red Sox stumble against the Rockies was one of those September games where motivation matters more than talent. I've seen it a hundred times.

## Looking Ahead to Saturday's Slate

Here's where experience comes into play. The Mets-Nationals rematch is our top pick for September 27th, and yes, I know we just missed on Washington yesterday. But this is a different pitching matchup, and sometimes the best play is going right back to the well.

Sean Manaea gets the ball for New York, and he's been one of those steady September performers who knows how to navigate lineups this time of year. DJ Herz for Washington? He's got talent, but I've seen enough young arms hit the wall in late September to know where the edge is here.

content.title: ⭐ Saturday's Top Pick - Sep 27
content.sub: Pick: New York Mets (52%) • Manaea vs Herz • First pitch Saturday

content.value:
## The September Factor

You know what I love about late September baseball? The narratives write themselves, but the numbers don't lie. The Mets are playing meaningful games right now. Washington's playing out the string. That 52% confidence might look thin on paper, but factor in the context—the urgency, the veteran presence, the pitching edge—and this is exactly the kind of spot where experience beats raw talent.

I've been around long enough to know that a coin flip game with context becomes a 55-45 edge real quick. And that's all we need.

See you tomorrow with the full slate breakdown. Let's keep this thing rolling.
